newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas prices soar to year-highs.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas prices soar to year-highs.

text.p: Spot natural gas prices in Alberta soared on Wednesday to new year-high levels, as bone-chilling temperatures in western Canada continued and prices strengthened across the continent.
Spot prices at Alberta's AECO storage facility climbed as high as C$2.75 per gigajoule in early trade, before settling back to C$2.65 per GJ. AECO gas was quoted at C$2.13/2.18 per GJ on Tuesday.
"It's exceeding my expectations -- it's nuts," said a marketing manager with a Calgary-based producer.
"It's up a nickel after each trade," said another trader.
Players were hard-pressed to recall the last time Alberta prices were at current levels. AECO gas climbed to C$2.25 per GJ during the peak days of last winter.

The sharp runup in prices was the result of several factors, including forecasts for continued icy western Canadian weather, lower-than-expected delivery receipts on the NOVA intra-Alberta pipeline network, strong demand from the western part of North America and the booming NYMEX December price, which climbed on Wednesday to above US$3.50 per million British thermal units.

"But there are enough fundamentals locally to keep the price up," said the marketing manager. The temperature in southern Alberta hovered at -24 Celsius (-11 Fahrenheit) on Wednesday, and lows of -28 Celsius (-18 Fahrenheit) with snow flurries were expected through the weekend, said Environment Canada.
Gas withdrawals at all three Alberta storage facilities were said to be totalling 1.1 billion cubic feet per day.
Peter Linder, analyst with CIBC Woody Gundy, said Canadian gas producers were in the unusual position of making profitable deals in the Alberta spot market.

Because of Alberta's scarcity of pipeline space to richer U.S. markets, only those producers with long-term capacity on pipelines to the Midwest and Northeast were able to reap the benefits of high prices last year.
This year, producers with export space are getting "excellent" prices and those selling in Alberta are getting "great" prices, Linder said.
He said that he reckoned producers were receiving an average gas price of C$2.75 per thousand cubic feet. Most analyst forecasts for the 1997 are between C$1.60 and C$1.80 per MCF.
Renaissance Energy Ltd, among the leaders of Canada's gas producers this year for average price, was likely receiving over C$4 per MCF, Linder said.
He said his top stock pick among Canadian companies benefitting from current gas prices was Anderson Exploration Ltd.
